title: Cannot generate PCK Encrypted Templates > Android NDK28 and CXX/Clang++ incompat¿?
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible with Godot 4.5dev5.
-Problem is > NDK28 <

### System information

Debian (trixie)

### Issue description

I'm trying to generate PCK Encrypted Templates, 
just to be able to use Godot 4.5dev5 and solve the 16KB Memory problem with Android 14/15.

"Android: Add support for 16 KB page sizes, update to NDK r28b ([GH-106358](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106358))."

Very Important!

However...
-Apparently the CXX/Clang++ related stuff has changed from NDK27 to NDK28, considerable structural changes.

It seems the CXX/Clang++ related stuff in the Official Android NDK28 is Different from what Scons expects.

That makes the Scons build fail directly.


-You cannot make the NDK28 build use the Clang from NDK27.

And I'm not experienced enough to make Scons use a let's say, custom or system-wide version of Clang,
or fix it in any way possible..

So I cannot find a solution..
Gemini AI understands the problem, but cannot fix it.

### Steps to reproduce

Simple!

Get NDK28:
https://developer.android.com/ndk/downloads

Place it where it needs to be:
```
~/Android/Sdk/ndk➤ ls                                                                       
23.1.7779620  23.2.8568313  25.1.8937393  25.2.9519653  27.2.12479018  28.1.13356709
```

-Get the Godot repo from Github:
```
git clone https://github.com/godotengine/godot.git godot-source-4.5dev5
cd godot-source-4.5dev5

git checkout 64b09905c7b2877f8aef99d8b63e73e5d31acfb9

git submodule update --init --recursive
```

-Set the Environ:
```
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk"
export ANDROID_NDK_ROOT="$HOME/Android/Sdk/ndk/28.1.13356709"
export PATH="$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$PATH"
export PATH="$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$PATH"
export SCRIPT_AES256_ENCRYPTION_KEY="YOUR_AES_KEY_HERE"
export GODOT_VERSION_STATUS="dev5.mono"  ### Do I need to put .mono?
```

-You can Clean, just in case
```
scons --clean platform=android target=template_release
scons --clean platform=android target=template_debug
```

And make the Templates:
```
scons platform=android android_arch=arm64 target=template_release production=yes generate_apk=yes
scons platform=android android_arch=armv7 target=template_release production=yes
scons platform=android android_arch=x86_64 target=template_release production=yes

scons platform=android android_arch=arm64 target=template_debug generate_apk=yes
scons platform=android android_arch=armv7 target=template_debug
scons platform=android android_arch=x86_64 target=template_debug 
```


-Problem n1 > Missing Swappy:

```
PCK Templates/Godot 4.5dev5/godot-source-4.5dev5➤ scons --clean platform=android target=template_release
scons --clean platform=android target=template_debug

scons: Reading SConscript files ...
Auto-detected 8 CPU cores available for build parallelism. Using 7 cores by default. You can override it with the `-j` or `num_jobs` arguments.
WARNING: Swappy Frame Pacing not detected! It is strongly recommended you download it from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-swappy/releases and extract it so that the following files can be found:

Without Swappy, Godot apps on Android will inevitable suffer stutter and struggle to keep consistent 30/60/90/120 fps. Though Swappy cannot guarantee your app will be stutter-free, not having Swappy will guarantee there will be stutter even on the best phones and the most simple of scenes.
```

Swappy is Missing!!

Good, let's fix that..

/whatever/PCK Templates/Godot 4.5dev5/godot-source-4.5dev5

```

cp -r "/whatever/PCK Templates/swappy/godot-swappy/arm64-v8a" thirdparty/swappy-frame-pacing/
```

-Swappy is Fixed.

The CXX or clang++ stuff is Wrong.

But this is not a problem with the Templates..
It's a problem with NDK28!!!!!!!!!!!


-Here's the NDK's:
https://developer.android.com/ndk/downloads

If you get them and go to the folder:
Android/Sdk/ndk/27.2.12479018/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/

or

/Android/Sdk/ndk/28.1.13356709/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/

You'll find everything Clang related.
